title: Review: Particle accelerators and detectors; Particles, antiparticles and classification; Pair production and annihilation; Fundamental interactions and exchange particles; Conservation laws in particle interactions; Estimation and orders of magnitude
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: P01-uk2#t4 term and clue written for the game; P01-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; P02-2#t3 term and clue written for the game; P02-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MS04-1#N.10, P03-1#N.13a, P04-1#N.14, P05-1#N.4, MS04-1#N.6, P03-1#N.8, P04-1#N.9, P05-1#N.13, MS04-1#N.3, P03-1#N.3b, P04-1#N.8, P05-1#N.2. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Negative pion
items.clue: Meson made of a down quark and an anti-up quark, charge –1.

items.label: Baryon
items.clue: Particle made of three quarks, such as a proton or a neutron.

items.label: Beta-minus decay
items.clue: A down quark becomes an up quark, so a neutron becomes a proton.

items.label: Gravitational interaction
items.clue: Acts on all mass; infinite range; by far the feeblest of the four.

questions.stem: A classroom is about 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. What is the order of magnitude of the mass of air in it?
questions.explanation: Volume ≈ 8 × 6 × 3 = 144 m³. Mass ≈ 144 × 1.2 ≈ 170 kg, order 10² kg.

questions.stem: Which of these proposed interactions is forbidden by a conservation law?
questions.explanation: Q 0 = 0 and B 1 = 1, but L: 0 + 1 = +1 before, 0 − 1 = −1 after. Electron capture emits a neutrino, νₑ, not an antineutrino.

questions.stem: A ring's bending magnets already run at their maximum field. Engineers want protons with three times the momentum. What must they do?

options.text: Build a ring with nine times the bending radius, since kinetic energy goes as momentum squared.
Build a smaller ring, since faster protons are easier to steer.
Build a ring with three times the bending radius.
Keep the ring and add more accelerating cavities.

questions.explanation: Radius = momentum ÷ (B × charge). B cannot rise, so the radius must rise in proportion: three times the momentum, three times the radius.

questions.stem: A muon and an antimuon, both almost at rest, annihilate to produce two photons. The rest energy of a muon is 105.7 MeV. What is the wavelength of each photon?
What is the best estimate of the volume of water in a full bath?
questions.explanation: About 1.5 m × 0.6 m × 0.4 m ≈ 0.4 m³ (about 400 litres).

questions.stem: A student proposes that a free neutron decays into a proton and an electron and nothing else: n → p + e⁻. Which conservation law that holds in all nuclear decays would this proposal break?

options.text: Charge, since two charged particles would come from one neutral particle
Baryon number, since a neutron would be replaced by a proton
Lepton number, since the number of electrons and neutrinos would rise
Mass, since the proton and electron have less mass than the neutron

questions.stem: Two protons each gain the same energy on one lap. One was moving at 0.50c, the other at 0.99c. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Both speeds rise by the same amount, since both gain the same energy.
The faster proton's speed rises more, since it is already moving quickly.
The slower proton's speed rises more; the faster one's speed barely changes.
Neither speed changes; the energy only raises their relativistic mass.

questions.explanation: At 0.50c the speed still rises noticeably. At 0.99c the energy raises the momentum (in CCEA's terms, the relativistic mass), not the speed.

questions.stem: An electron and a positron, each with 0.30 MeV of kinetic energy, collide head-on and annihilate into two photons. The rest energy of an electron is 0.511 MeV. What is the energy of each photon?
questions.explanation: Head-on with equal energies, the total momentum is zero, so the two photons have equal energies and fly apart in opposite directions. Each: 0.511 + 0.30 = 0.81 MeV.

questions.stem: Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × speed². What is the order of magnitude of the kinetic energy of an adult walking?
questions.explanation: ½ × 70 kg × (1.5 m s⁻¹)² ≈ 80 J, nearest power of ten 10² J.

questions.stem: Two protons collide at high energy: p + p → p + n + X, where X stands for all the other particles produced. What must the total charge of X be?
questions.explanation: Before: +1 + 1 = +2e. After: +1 + 0 + X. Charge is conserved, so X = +1e (for example a positron with a neutrino, or a positive pion).

questions.stem: Protons circulate in a synchrotron at constant energy. A fault makes the field of the bending magnets fall slightly. What happens to the protons?

options.text: They slow down, because the magnets no longer push them as hard.
Their paths curve less, so they drift outwards towards the wall of the beam pipe.
Their paths curve more, so they spiral inwards.
They stay on the same circle, because a magnetic force does no work.

questions.explanation: r = mv/(Bq). Same momentum, smaller B, so a larger radius: the beam moves off the ring.

questions.stem: An electron and a positron annihilate, producing two photons. Which quantity is different after the annihilation from before it?
questions.explanation: Photons have no rest mass. The pair's mass has been converted to photon energy, but energy and momentum are conserved.
